text:
Oliver: Quick heads-up — new reranker v3 bringup shows a weird split when we bucket by answer density. float NDCG@10 slightly up, but MRR drops on high-density queries :thinking_face:
Neha: can you drop the bucketed numbers?
Oliver: sure, paste from the eval run below (rounded)
```
Baseline float32 (v2):
  NDCG@10  low: 0.432  mid: 0.451  high: 0.478
  MRR      low: 0.220  mid: 0.205  high: 0.190
Quantized hybrid (v3-int8-hybrid):
  NDCG@10  low: 0.435  mid: 0.449  high: 0.465
  MRR      low: 0.222  mid: 0.198  high: 0.165
Delta (v3 - v2):
  NDCG@10  +0.003  -0.002  -0.013
  MRR      +0.002  -0.007  -0.025
```
Oliver: so NDCG moves are small but MRR collapse in high-density bucket is larger than I'd expect.
Sam: interesting — MRR is more sensitive to top-of-list reorderings, could be ties/score quantization or candidate pruning differences. did you check tie-breaking/stable-sort?
Oliver: yes, we kept the same tie-breaker (doc id). I also ran with `--preserve-score-precision` to force float scoring at rank-time and saw the MRR loss shrink to ~-0.01 in high bucket.
Tara: could this be label granularity? high-density queries have multiple labeled answers per doc; NDCG can reward later positions while MRR only looks at first hit. if quantization pushes a good doc from #1 to #2 we lose MRR but NDCG barely changes.
Neha: good point. do we have answer-span counts per query in the holdout?
Oliver: yes — high bucket avg spans/query = 3.2, mid = 1.4, low = 0.6.
Neha: action: run a targeted holdout where we collapse multi-span labels to a single canonical span per query and re-eval MRR vs NDCG. also run with candidate order-preserving rescoring to see if KVcache/packing affects relative scores.
Sam: +1. also try reranking without passage-splitting (treat doc as single chunk) to see if chunking-induced candidate duplicates are changing top1.
Tara: i can check label duplication / gold aggregation rules. I recall our ingestion deduped by url but allowed multiple spans to be separate candidates. if the quantized model scores duplicates differently we'll see this effect.
Oliver: I kicked off 3 quick experiments in preprod:
- `eval/score_split_preservefloat --split=answer_density --buckets=low,mid,high`
- `eval/collapse_golds --strategy=first_span_per_query`
- `eval/no_chunking_rerank --chunk_method=none`
ci-bot: Preprod run queued: https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/13579 (results ETA ~20m) :eyes:
Neha: thanks. once CI finishes, let's collect per-query top-k hit positions and plot difference (delta position histogram) — that should show whether many queries shift by 1 spot (MRR sensitive) vs many small rank jitter (NDCG less sensitive).
Sam: if it is quantization-induced score compression, a simple temperature/rescaling layer on logits after the scorer could recover top1. try `logit_scale=1.2` as a quick probe.
Tara: also verify candidate dedupe at eval-time: we should dedupe identical text+url before computing MRR.
Oliver: agreed. I'll open an internal ticket with the run ids and a short repro note and tag analytics for per-query histograms.
Neha: perfect. follow-ups: if collapse_golds removes the discrepancy, we should update our evaluation docs to standardize gold aggregation (and warn on MRR fragility for multi-ans queries).
Oliver: thanks team. will post CI link and attach csvs when done. :pray:
